meta.title: Run Lab
meta.description: Play with running form and breathing: pace, posture, terrain, and how the club runs them.

playground.title: Run Lab
playground.intro: Move a dial, watch the runner, read the note. The see-through one is the Pacer.

loading.still: Still loading — the runner is about half a megabyte.

fallback.noWebgl: Your browser can't draw the runner, but the notes still work — every dial explains itself.
fallback.reducedMotion: Motion is reduced in your settings — scrub through the stride instead.

pacer.label: Pacer
pacer.tooltip: A see-through clubmate running the ideal form for this ground.

notes.easy: Conversational — you could chat the whole way. Most of the club's weekly runs live here.
notes.steady: Comfortable, but you'd keep your sentences short. A good place to feel your form settle.
notes.tempo: Controlled hard. Breathing gets loud; cadence climbs before stride does.
notes.fast: Race pace and above. Everything gets bigger — stride, arm swing, breath. Form holds if the basics do.

lean.label: Forward lean

notes.low: Standing tall is fine; sitting back behind your feet makes every step a small brake. Try tipping from the ankles, not the hips.
notes.ideal: A slight lean from the ankles, like you're about to fall forward and keep catching it. Gravity does a little of the work.
notes.high: Folding at the waist puts the lean in your back, not your ankles. Most people find it tires the lower back and shortens the breath.

lean.description: From sitting back to folded forward

footstrike.label: Footstrike

notes.low: Landing out in front, heel first, means the ground pushes back before you're over it. Try shorter, quicker steps and let the foot land closer to under you.
notes.ideal: The foot lands roughly under your hips, flat-ish, and rolls through. Quiet landing, less braking.
notes.high: Up on the toes with tiny steps works for a sprint, less for a Wednesday 10K. Most people's calves let them know.

footstrike.description: From reaching out to on the toes

arms.label: Arm swing

notes.low: Hands crossing the centre line twist your torso a little every step, and your legs follow. Try thinking 'elbows back' instead of 'hands forward'.
notes.ideal: Elbows around ninety degrees, hands relaxed, swinging front to back past your hips. The swing balances the legs; it doesn't drive them.
notes.high: Perfectly parallel, locked arms are a lot of effort for very little. A little natural drift is fine — you're not a piston.

arms.description: From crossing over to locked straight

notes.low: Shoulders creeping toward your ears is the classic tired-runner tell. Shake your hands out, drop the shoulders, carry an imaginary crisp in each fist.
notes.ideal: Shoulders low and loose, chest open, hands soft. Check them every kilometre or so — they drift when you stop thinking about them.
notes.high: Letting the shoulders slump forward closes the chest, and a closed chest takes a shallower breath. Loose is not the same as collapsed.

gaze.label: Gaze

notes.low: Looking at your feet tips the head forward and the whole spine follows. Your feet know where the ground is.
notes.ideal: Eyes about twenty to thirty metres down the path. The head sits over the shoulders and the neck stays long.
notes.high: Chin up at the horizon arches the back and strains the neck. Look ahead, not up — the sky isn't going anywhere.

gaze.description: From at your feet to at the sky

notes.low: Energy spent going up is energy not going forward. Bouncing usually comes with a slow cadence — try quicker, lighter steps and let the head stay level.
notes.ideal: The head stays almost level; the horizon barely moves. A little spring is right — you're running, not gliding.
notes.high: Shuffling with no spring at all keeps you low but makes every step a scuff. Let the ankle do a little bouncing for you.

track.label: Track
track.note: Flat, soft, measured. The place to feel what your form does with nothing else going on.
track.caption: Lane 3. Anticlockwise, like everyone.

riverside.label: Riverside
riverside.note: The club's home ground. Flat and long — it rewards a relaxed rhythm more than anything clever.
riverside.caption: Home turf. Headwind on the way back.

trail.label: Trail
trail.note: Every step is a small decision. Shorter steps, eyes a little closer, arms out a touch for balance — it's a quest, not a time trial.
trail.caption: Mind the roots.

uphill.label: Uphill
uphill.note: Shorten the step, lift the knees a little, lean into it from the ankles. Effort up, pace down — that's the deal.
uphill.caption: It ends. Eventually.

downhill.label: Downhill
downhill.note: The instinct is to lean back and brake with your heels. Try the opposite: quick light steps, hips over the feet, let the hill carry you.
downhill.caption: Quiet feet.

3-2.note: Five steps a cycle, so the exhale — the moment you're least braced — lands on the left foot one cycle and the right the next. Neither side takes all of it.

2-2.note: Four steps a cycle, easy to hold when the effort climbs. The exhale always lands on the same foot; some people switch feet every few minutes.

2-1.note: Three steps a cycle for when you need air fast. Still odd, so the exhale keeps alternating.

club.name: Club form
club.intro: How we'd run a Wednesday. Everything relaxed, nothing forced.

heel.name: Heel Striker
heel.intro: Reaches out and lands heel-first, well ahead of the hips. You can hear it on the riverside.

bouncer.name: Bouncer
bouncer.intro: Spends a lot of the run going up. Great for photos, slow for running.

shoulders.name: Tense Shoulders
shoulders.intro: Shoulders up by the ears, fists clenched. Usually turns up around kilometre eight.

arms.name: Cross-body Arms
arms.intro: Hands swing across the chest and the torso twists to keep up.

sitter.name: Sitter
sitter.intro: Hips behind the feet, like running toward a chair. Every step brakes a little.

gazer.name: Gazer
gazer.intro: Eyes on the shoes. The head drops, the back rounds, the breath gets short.

lines: That's the club's stride. See you Wednesday.
Loose hands, long neck. That's the one.
Head level, eyes down the path. See you at the river.

contact.label: Contact
contact.note: The foot meets the ground — ideally under you, not out in front.

midstance.label: Midstance
midstance.note: Full weight over one leg. Hip, knee and ankle stack; this is where a lean shows.

toeOff.label: Toe-off
toeOff.note: The ankle springs and the leg leaves the ground behind you. Push back, not up.

flight.label: Flight
flight.note: Both feet off the ground. Arms and legs swap; the head barely moves.

notes.component: Our everyday training tee: technical fabric, a close cut, nothing to think about on a recovery run.
notes.coda: Seventy-five grams of singlet for hot days and hard efforts. The deep armhole leaves the shoulders free to swing.
notes.hoole: Washed cotton in a boxy cut, from our collaboration with Furies. More community than kit, and it moves like it.
notes.communion: The Communion T rebuilt with New Balance in performance fabric, in a slightly relaxed cut.
